#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily auto-publish report (issue #161): renders the per-run job-summary
# table and drives the self-healing issue lifecycle.
#
#   failing/cancelled leg -> file a bug issue assigned to the owner; dedup
#     guard: an OPEN issue labeled `daily-publish` with the same title gets
#     a fresh comment (new run link + log excerpt) instead of a duplicate
#   green leg -> auto-close that leg's still-open issue with a comment
#
# Inputs come from environment (set by the daily-publish.yml report job):
#   PLAN_RESULT         needs.plan.result — a plan failure files its own issue
#   LEG_<NAME>          needs result: success | failure | skipped | cancelled
#   LEG_<NAME>_URL      child run URL (empty on internal/skip paths)
#   LEG_PUBDEV_*        status (up-to-date/private/recovered/release-in-flight),
#                       versions, tag-run URL
#   NEXT_TAG            estimated next tag (informational; legs derive latest+1 themselves)
#   GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL   runner defaults
#
# Exits non-zero when any leg failed or was cancelled (the daily run goes
# red too); all-skipped stays green (#159 lesson).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
next_tag="${NEXT_TAG:-}"
failed_legs=""
actions=""
rows="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT

gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── log collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Failing job/step names and the last ~50 log lines, from the child run when
# one exists, else from this daily run's leg job (jobs API — the run is
# still in progress here, and GitHub serves no logs for it mid-run).
failing_steps() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --json jobs --jq '
      [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
        | .name + " — " +
          ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
            | .name] | join(", "))]
      | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # The report job runs INSIDE the daily run, so the run is still in
    # progress here — and GitHub serves no logs for in-progress runs
    # (--log-failed returns empty: issue #208 was filed as "unknown (job
    # cancelled or timed out)" for a leg that died in 4s with a clear
    # error). Job/step data IS served mid-run — read failed steps from it.
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg job "$2" '
          [.jobs[] | select(.name == $job
                              and (.conclusion == "failure"
                                or .conclusion == "cancelled"))
            | .name + " — " +
              ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure"
                               or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                | .name] | join(", "))]
          | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null | tail -n 50 || true
  else
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | grep -F "$2" | tail -n 50 || true
  fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$prefix")

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    echo
    echo "Last lines of the failed step's log:"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'
  else
    local created
    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
}

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id
  local title="[daily-publish] $1 leg failed"
  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ leg \`$1\` went green again in $daily_url — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    actions+="auto-closed #${existing} ($1 green again)"$'\n'
  fi
}

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"

    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then

# when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window; or the
  # release-tag job has not cut the tag off a fresh bump yet) is classified
  # «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh — a neutral skip
  # (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled daily re-verifies.
  # The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml run» error one minute
  # before the healthy run completed (#1189, false alarm).

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)

        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the

  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that

  sweep-drafts:

      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1370
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1370
- **Title**: fix(1368): pub.dev publish — push-tag-only OIDC path, dart-only gate, verify waits instead of false-alarming
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1368-pubdev-oidc-verify` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +557
- **Deletions**: -129
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T07:00:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T08:26:11Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1368

## Root causes (drilled from the cited runs)

**Mechanism A — OIDC exit 65 + gated-off legitimate publisher.** Every tag fires ci.yml twice (push + release). pub.dev trusted publishing accepts **push/workflow_dispatch events only** (owner-verified console config) — so the release twin's `Publish to pub.dev` attempt always died `Authentication failed!` (exit 65): v1.0.520 release run 37517511975, publish job 112467963058 = failure. Meanwhile the push twin — the only OIDC-valid publisher — never ran: publish `needs` quality-gate's aggregate, and a red platform/PTY leg reddens it (v1.0.520 push run 37517510546: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` failure → Quality gate failure → `Publish to pub.dev` skipped). Same shape on v1.0.519 (runs 37496726750/37496726086). Legit publisher gated off, illegitimate publisher auth-fails → pub.dev frozen at 1.0.518.

**Mechanism B — verify race + false green.** Today's daily leg (run 37576546071, job 112647157034) read at 05:31:55, hit the no-tag branch, judged the 10.5h-old bump "wedged" (1h horizon) and errored `v1.0.521 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered`. release-tag cut the tag at 05:35:13 — 3 minutes later — and the v1.0.521 runs (37576955921 push / 37576956727 release) exist, still queued hours later on runner starvation. Separately, the old `release-in-flight` classification exited 0 and the daily report rendered it ✅ and auto-closed the leg's issue — yesterday's "Leg: pub.dev: success" while the publish had failed.

## Fix

1. **Publish from push-tag events only** — the release arm is removed from the `publish` `if` (the v0.1.370-402 lightweight-tag era it covered is gone; every tag is now PAT-pushed annotated, proven by the push twins on 519/520/521). A hypothetical release-only tag now skips publish and the daily verify alarms `only release-event run(s)` loudly.
2. **Publish gate is dart-only** — `quality-gate` exports `dart_ok` (verdict over the pure-Dart package legs: static, analyze, test-core, coverage, guards, flutter/faui tests, crap, integration-mock, hostile-env, supply-chain, dep-audit, perf/usage-fold). Platform/native/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos, fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) cannot redden `dart_ok` — but still redden the required aggregate. `integration` (Provider smoke, #551) runs off `dart_ok` instead of the aggregate result and stays a hard publish gate.
3. **Verify script** (`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`):
   - waits a bounded window (`TAG_APPEAR_WAIT_SECS`, 10m) for a pending tag to appear — any bump age is pending, the 1h wedge horizon is gone;
   - waits up to `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` (30m) for the push run to reach a terminal state before classifying (Never-again #1: poll with timeout);
   - selects the **push-event twin** for classification and recovery (`gh run rerun --failed` on the release twin can never publish);
   - every error names its state: `no tag and no chore(release) bump on main` / `only release-event run(s) exist` / `no run registered past the grace window` / `publish did not upload` (Never-again #2);
   - past any budget → neutral `release-in-flight` skip, never an error.
4. **Report** (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`): `release-in-flight` renders ⏭️ "skipped: release in flight (… outcome unobserved …)" — never ✅ — and does not close the leg's open issue; only a verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered) does.

## Tests

`test/release_flow_race_test.dart` extended: push-event fixtures, twin-selection, terminal-wait flip + budget lapse, tag-appear-mid-wait (lsremote-fail-first seam), release-only alarm, the #1368 10.5h-bump regression, plus ci.yml/report wiring pins. **Disclosure:** the dart VM is SIGKILLed on this host (exit 137, known machine guard), so the suite could not run locally; as a fallback I replicated the harness sandbox 1:1 in bash (same stub gh/curl/git semantics, 10 scenarios / 29 assertions — all pass) and smoke-ran the report renderer (⏭️ + zero issue lifecycle actions); both workflows re-validated as YAML. The dart suite itself gates this PR in CI.

## Honest boundary (owner/SM side)

- This PR fixes **future tags** (new SHAs carry the new ci.yml). **Acceptance #1 (pub.dev serves ≥1.0.521) is not met by this PR**: backfilling 1.0.519–1.0.521 needs the queued v1.0.521 push twin to finish green, or reruns/manual publish per the runbook — note `gh run rerun` of the old tags replays the OLD ci.yml (result-based gate), so a red leg on those SHAs can still block; SM-prioritized CI or a manual `dart pub publish` may be needed. Per the standing CI-dispatch ban I did not dispatch, rerun, or queue anything.
- pub.dev admin config needed no changes (owner already verified).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1370._

> ℹ️ **7 thread(s) already resolved and excluded from this review.**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 8

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The headline "dart-only publish gate" is inverted: platform/PTY legs are the ones that set `dart_ok=false` (so a red PTY shard still skips the publish — the v1.0.519–521 starvation persists unchanged), while package-red legs `fail` before `dart_ok` is ever exported (empty ≠ `'false'`), which makes the Provider smoke run on doomed runs. Three important issues: the new "only release-event run(s)" alarm bypasses the #1189 grace window and can false-alarm in the release-twin-first visibility race; the 30-min terminal-wait poll loop makes unguarded `gh run view` calls that turn one transient API blip into a filed issue; plus suggestions on stale `now`/negative tag ages, the 40m-of-waits vs 60m leg budget, and a missing EOF newline.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 ci.yml gate: `case` branches swapped vs the documented design (comment1) — blocking
- ⚠️ integration `if` `!= 'false'` + empty-output hole; release-only alarm bypasses grace; unguarded poll calls (comments 2–4)
- 💡 stale `now` after waits; leg-budget math; EOF newline (comments 5–7)

**Next Steps**:
1. Swap the gate branches: package red → `dart_ok=false` (deferred fail), platform red → keep `dart_ok=true`, fail the aggregate after export; update the test pins that enshrine the current pattern
2. Gate the release-only alarm behind the grace window + spaced re-read; harden poll-loop `gh` calls with retry/continue
3. Note: acceptance #1 (pub.dev serves ≥1.0.521) is correctly disclosed as out of scope; the removal of the never-cut-tag wedge backstop is a deliberate tradeoff that now relies entirely on `auto_release.sh`'s own wedge alarm — worth a line in `docs/ci.md`

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the dart-only gate is inverted — the exact starvation this PR fixes still happens**

The documented design (PR description, the comments below, and the test reason strings) is: *platform/native/PTY legs "cannot redden `dart_ok`" — only package legs may redden it*. The implementation does the opposite — **the two `case` branches are swapped**:

- **Platform leg red** (this branch) sets `dart_ok=false` → the publish job's `needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true'` is false → **publish skips**. The v1.0.520 shape (red `pty-integration-linux` shard on the push twin) produces byte-for-byte the same outcome as the old result-based gate. Fix #2 is a no-op as implemented.
- **Package leg red** hits `fail` inside the loop, so the step exits **before** `echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` ever runs → the exported output is **empty**, not `false`.

Simulated against the step body verbatim:

```text
A: PTY leg red      → exported [dart_ok=false] → publish SKIPS (starvation persists), smoke skips
B: package leg red  → exported [] (nothing)    → publish SKIPS (ok), but smoke RUNS (see the integration-if comment)
```

To implement the documented behavior: in the loop, **package** legs must set `dart_ok=false` (deferred — do not `fail` inside the loop), and **platform** legs must leave `dart_ok=true` (track a separate `platform_red=true`); then export `dart_ok`, and fail the aggregate afterwards if either `dart_ok != true` or `platform_red`. That keeps the aggregate red (branch protection unchanged) while letting the push twin publish.

Note: `test/release_flow_race_test.dart`'s new pins assert the swapped pattern list verbatim ("every platform/native/PTY leg must be publish-exempt" while pinning exactly the list that reddens it) — they must be updated together with this fix, otherwise CI re-enshrines the bug.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `dart_ok != 'false'` lets the smoke run on a package-red (doomed) run — empty output ≠ `false`**

When a **package** leg is red, the gate step `fail`s before exporting `dart_ok`, so `needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok` is `''`, not `'false'`. This `if` therefore evaluates `'' != 'false'` → **true**, and the 20-minute real-provider smoke (real `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/… spend) runs on a tag run whose publish can never start (`dart_ok == 'true'` is false for `''`).

This contradicts the comment right below ("dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the publish it gates cannot run anyway") — that only holds for the platform-red path, where `dart_ok=false` is actually exported.

Two clean fixes (either suffices; do the first if you take the comment1 fix):
1. Export `dart_ok=false` for package-red too (deferred fail) — then `!= 'false'` behaves as documented.
2. Make this condition `!= 'true'` so the smoke runs only when the pure-Dart verdict is explicitly green.

The publish job is unaffected either way (it requires `== 'true'`), so this is wasted-runner/LLM-spend plus comment-accuracy, not a publish-safety bug.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "only release-event run(s)" alarm fires on the first read, bypassing the grace window — reintroduces the #1189 false-alarm class**

The grace window (AC1) exists precisely because a freshly pushed tag's ci.yml run can lag **minutes** in API visibility (#1189: tag 05:32, verify read "no run" at 05:35, healthy run completed 05:37). For PAT-pushed tags, release-tag publishes the GitHub Release essentially concurrently with the tag push, so the **release twin can become API-visible while the push twin has not registered yet**. In that window this branch alarms `never triggered (only release-event run(s) exist …)`, exits 1, and the daily self-files an issue — a false alarm of exactly the class this PR exists to kill. The grace `in_flight` skip is now only reachable when *no* runs at all exist, and the same bypass repeats on the second read (line 205).

Suggested fix: only arm the release-only alarm **past the grace window and after the spaced re-read** — i.e. move both `any_run_of` checks to after the `tag_age -lt grace` / re-read logic (a young release-only list → neutral `in_flight`; an old one → alarm). Also note `workflow_dispatch` runs on the tag ref land in this same alarm but pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC — the message text ("only release-event run(s)") would be wrong there; consider "non-push run(s)".

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: unguarded `gh run view` inside the 30-minute poll loop — one transient API failure aborts the leg as an error**

Under `set -euo pipefail`, a single transient `gh`/network failure (502, blip, secondary rate limit) on this line kills the script mid-wait, fails the leg, and the report job files "[daily-publish] pub.dev leg failed" — a false alarm re-introduced through the new polling path (up to 90 sequential API calls per wait, ×2 waits). Everywhere else the script defends against this (three spaced pub.dev reads, `curl --retry 3`, the AC1 re-read); this new loop is the least fault-tolerant network call in the file.

Suggested fix: tolerate failed polls as "still pending" and only alarm/skip on budget lapse:

```bash
if ! status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null); then
  echo "transient gh failure polling run $run_id (attempt $attempt/$attempts)"
  attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
  continue
fi
```

(The follow-up `conclusion=$(gh run view …)` after the loop has the same exposure but is pre-existing; hardening it too while you are here would be cheap.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `now` is sampled once at script start — tag ages go stale (even negative) after the waits**

`now=$(date +%s)` (line 113) is fixed, but `read_tag_age` is called again inside this appear-wait loop. If the tag is cut *during* the wait, `tag_age = now - creatordate` goes **negative** (the tag is newer than the snapshot). Downstream the grace check `[ "$tag_age" -lt "$grace" ]` then renders notices like `v1.0.521 exists (-540s old < 900s grace)` and takes the neutral-skip path — fail-safe direction, but the negative age is confusing in the leg notice/su…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/S…

integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Issue #551: the ONLY tag-only LLM job — a small provider smoke.
      # `--tags "integration && llm"` selects the real-provider files
      # (anthropic / google / openrouter / ollama round-trips; copilot,
      # chatgpt-codex and subagent-real-model self-skip without their
      # creds). The 50-file integration suite itself runs per-PR now
      # (integration-mock + nightly pty-integration): tag CI no longer
      # gates releases on it, publish waits on this smoke instead.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart test --tags "integration && llm"
        run: dart test --tags "integration && llm"

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Install quickjs-ng
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs" \
            https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs/releases/download/v0.16.2/qjs-linux-x86_64
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: dart test --tags integration (qjs engine suites)
        run: dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/

  publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    #
    # #1368, two changes:
    # 1. PUSH-EVENT TAGS ONLY. pub.dev trusted publishing accepts OIDC tokens
    #    from push and workflow_dispatch events ONLY — there is no
    #    release-event option (owner verified the pub.dev console). The old
    #    release arm made the release-event twin of every tag ATTEMPT the
    #    publish whenever the push twin had not uploaded — pub.dev rejected
    #    the token's event claim and the leg died "Authentication failed!"
    #    (exit 65) on every release since the gate graph grew legs that can
    #    redden the push twin. The v0.1.370-402 era this arm once covered

    #    is PAT-pushed annotated (release-tag/auto_release), so the push twin
    #    always exists. A release-only tag would now skip publish and the
    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate
    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-

      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')

      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # A tag is a release announcement: if pubspec says publish_to: none,
      # failing LOUDLY is correct (#554) — a green skip is how pub.dev went
      # 35 versions stale unnoticed. Removing the flag from pubspec re-enables.
      - id: gate
        name: Publish gate
        run: |
          if grep -Eq '^publish_to:[[:space:]]*none' pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::pubspec.yaml sets publish_to: none — a tagged release cannot reach pub.dev. Remove the flag from pubspec.yaml, or stop tagging v* releases (see #554)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "publishable=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version — the daily-publish pubdev leg's
# check (gh-1192). Extracted verbatim from the inline step in
# daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness testable (fake
# gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the pubspec version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · the release-tag job has not cut the tag off the
#                           bump yet — at ANY bump age (the old 1h «wedge»
#                           horizon false-alarmed #1368: the verify read
#                           «never triggered» 3 minutes before the tag
#                           landed, off a 10.5h-old bump that self-healed on
#                           the next green main run); the script now WAITS a
#                           bounded window for the tag to appear
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner
#                           starvation may hold a queued run for hours
#                         · the tag is not cut yet but the bump commit is
#                           on main (release-tag pending)
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)»
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# E2: only the tag matching the CURRENT pubspec version is evaluated; stale
# older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
tag_appear_wait="${TAG_APPEAR_WAIT_SECS:-600}"      # wait for a pending tag cut
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits are
# sized so the leg always finishes INSIDE the wall — appear-wait 10m +
# terminal-wait 15m = 25m, or appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m +
# post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m. A job killed at 60m is a CANCELLED leg
# the report files as a watcher death — the «past any budget → neutral skip,
# never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else
    a="$max_polls"
  fi
  if [ "$a" -gt "$max_polls" ]; then a="$max_polls"; fi
  if [ "$a" -lt 1 ]; then a=1; fi
  echo "$a"
}

pubspec=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
emit "pubspec=$pubspec"
emit "published=" # re-exported below after query

if grep -q '^publish_to: *none' pubspec.yaml; then
  emit "status=private"
  echo "::notice::pubspec declares publish_to: none — package is private, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0
fi

# pub.dev API reads lag minutes behind a fresh publish (CDN replicas) — a
# single stale read must not send us into recovery. Three spaced reads, take
# the newest by version.
published=""
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
    https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version')
  published=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$published" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
  [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
done
emit "published=$published"
echo "pubspec=$pubspec published=$published"
newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pubspec" "$published" | sort -V | tail -1)
if [ "$newest" = "$published" ]; then
  emit "status=up-to-date"
  echo "::notice::pub.dev already serves $published"
  exit 0
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. PUSH and workflow_dispatch events carry OIDC tokens
# pub.dev accepts; the release-event twin can never publish (#1368) —
# classification and recovery use a publishable run, never the release twin.
# One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily auto-publish report (issue #161): renders the per-run job-summary
# table and drives the self-healing issue lifecycle.
#
#   failing/cancelled leg -> file a bug issue assigned to the owner; dedup
#     guard: an OPEN issue labeled `daily-publish` with the same title gets
#     a fresh comment (new run link + log excerpt) instead of a duplicate
#   green leg -> auto-close that leg's still-open issue with a comment
#
# Inputs come from environment (set by the daily-publish.yml report job):
#   PLAN_RESULT         needs.plan.result — a plan failure files its own issue
#   LEG_<NAME>          needs result: success | failure | skipped | cancelled
#   LEG_<NAME>_URL      child run URL (empty on internal/skip paths)
#   LEG_PUBDEV_*        status (up-to-date/private/recovered/release-in-flight),
#                       versions, tag-run URL
#   NEXT_TAG            estimated next tag (informational; legs derive latest+1 themselves)
#   GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL   runner defaults
#
# Exits non-zero when any leg failed or was cancelled (the daily run goes
# red too); all-skipped stays green (#159 lesson).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
next_tag="${NEXT_TAG:-}"
failed_legs=""
actions=""
rows="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT

gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── log collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Failing job/step names and the last ~50 log lines, from the child run when
# one exists, else from this daily run's leg job (jobs API — the run is
# still in progress here, and GitHub serves no logs for it mid-run).
failing_steps() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --json jobs --jq '
      [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
        | .name + " — " +
          ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
            | .name] | join(", "))]
      | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # The report job runs INSIDE the daily run, so the run is still in
    # progress here — and GitHub serves no logs for in-progress runs
    # (--log-failed returns empty: issue #208 was filed as "unknown (job
    # cancelled or timed out)" for a leg that died in 4s with a clear
    # error). Job/step data IS served mid-run — read failed steps from it.
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg job "$2" '
          [.jobs[] | select(.name == $job
                              and (.conclusion == "failure"
                                or .conclusion == "cancelled"))
            | .name + " — " +
              ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure"
                               or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                | .name] | join(", "))]
          | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null | tail -n 50 || true
  else
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | grep -F "$2" | tail -n 50 || true
  fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$prefix")

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    echo
    echo "Last lines of the failed step's log:"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'
  else
    local created
    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
}

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id
  local title="[daily-publish] $1 leg failed"
  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ leg \`$1\` went green again in $daily_url — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    actions+="auto-closed #${existing} ($1 green again)"$'\n'
  fi
}

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then
    if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then
      link_cell="$links"

  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window; or the
  # release-tag job has not cut the tag off a fresh bump yet) is classified
  # «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh — a neutral skip
  # (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled daily re-verifies.
  # The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml run» error one minute
  # before the healthy run completed (#1189, false alarm).

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).

  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1370
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1370
- **Title**: fix(1368): pub.dev publish — push-tag-only OIDC path, dart-only gate, verify waits instead of false-alarming
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1368-pubdev-oidc-verify` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +557
- **Deletions**: -129
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T07:00:48Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T08:26:11Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1368

## Root causes (drilled from the cited runs)

**Mechanism A — OIDC exit 65 + gated-off legitimate publisher.** Every tag fires ci.yml twice (push + release). pub.dev trusted publishing accepts **push/workflow_dispatch events only** (owner-verified console config) — so the release twin's `Publish to pub.dev` attempt always died `Authentication failed!` (exit 65): v1.0.520 release run 37517511975, publish job 112467963058 = failure. Meanwhile the push twin — the only OIDC-valid publisher — never ran: publish `needs` quality-gate's aggregate, and a red platform/PTY leg reddens it (v1.0.520 push run 37517510546: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` failure → Quality gate failure → `Publish to pub.dev` skipped). Same shape on v1.0.519 (runs 37496726750/37496726086). Legit publisher gated off, illegitimate publisher auth-fails → pub.dev frozen at 1.0.518.

**Mechanism B — verify race + false green.** Today's daily leg (run 37576546071, job 112647157034) read at 05:31:55, hit the no-tag branch, judged the 10.5h-old bump "wedged" (1h horizon) and errored `v1.0.521 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered`. release-tag cut the tag at 05:35:13 — 3 minutes later — and the v1.0.521 runs (37576955921 push / 37576956727 release) exist, still queued hours later on runner starvation. Separately, the old `release-in-flight` classification exited 0 and the daily report rendered it ✅ and auto-closed the leg's issue — yesterday's "Leg: pub.dev: success" while the publish had failed.

## Fix

1. **Publish from push-tag events only** — the release arm is removed from the `publish` `if` (the v0.1.370-402 lightweight-tag era it covered is gone; every tag is now PAT-pushed annotated, proven by the push twins on 519/520/521). A hypothetical release-only tag now skips publish and the daily verify alarms `only release-event run(s)` loudly.
2. **Publish gate is dart-only** — `quality-gate` exports `dart_ok` (verdict over the pure-Dart package legs: static, analyze, test-core, coverage, guards, flutter/faui tests, crap, integration-mock, hostile-env, supply-chain, dep-audit, perf/usage-fold). Platform/native/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos, fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) cannot redden `dart_ok` — but still redden the required aggregate. `integration` (Provider smoke, #551) runs off `dart_ok` instead of the aggregate result and stays a hard publish gate.
3. **Verify script** (`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`):
   - waits a bounded window (`TAG_APPEAR_WAIT_SECS`, 10m) for a pending tag to appear — any bump age is pending, the 1h wedge horizon is gone;
   - waits up to `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` (30m) for the push run to reach a terminal state before classifying (Never-again #1: poll with timeout);
   - selects the **push-event twin** for classification and recovery (`gh run rerun --failed` on the release twin can never publish);
   - every error names its state: `no tag and no chore(release) bump on main` / `only release-event run(s) exist` / `no run registered past the grace window` / `publish did not upload` (Never-again #2);
   - past any budget → neutral `release-in-flight` skip, never an error.
4. **Report** (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`): `release-in-flight` renders ⏭️ "skipped: release in flight (… outcome unobserved …)" — never ✅ — and does not close the leg's open issue; only a verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered) does.

## Tests

`test/release_flow_race_test.dart` extended: push-event fixtures, twin-selection, terminal-wait flip + budget lapse, tag-appear-mid-wait (lsremote-fail-first seam), release-only alarm, the #1368 10.5h-bump regression, plus ci.yml/report wiring pins. **Disclosure:** the dart VM is SIGKILLed on this host (exit 137, known machine guard), so the suite could not run locally; as a fallback I replicated the harness sandbox 1:1 in bash (same stub gh/curl/git semantics, 10 scenarios / 29 assertions — all pass) and smoke-ran the report renderer (⏭️ + zero issue lifecycle actions); both workflows re-validated as YAML. The dart suite itself gates this PR in CI.

## Honest boundary (owner/SM side)

- This PR fixes **future tags** (new SHAs carry the new ci.yml). **Acceptance #1 (pub.dev serves ≥1.0.521) is not met by this PR**: backfilling 1.0.519–1.0.521 needs the queued v1.0.521 push twin to finish green, or reruns/manual publish per the runbook — note `gh run rerun` of the old tags replays the OLD ci.yml (result-based gate), so a red leg on those SHAs can still block; SM-prioritized CI or a manual `dart pub publish` may be needed. Per the standing CI-dispatch ban I did not dispatch, rerun, or queue anything.
- pub.dev admin config needed no changes (owner already verified).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The headline "dart-only publish gate" is inverted: platform/PTY legs are the ones that set `dart_ok=false` (so a red PTY shard still skips the publish — the v1.0.519–521 starvation persists unchanged), while package-red legs `fail` before `dart_ok` is ever exported (empty ≠ `'false'`), which makes the Provider smoke run on doomed runs. Three important issues: the new "only release-event run(s)" alarm bypasses the #1189 grace window and can false-alarm in the release-twin-first visibility race; the 30-min terminal-wait poll loop makes unguarded `gh run view` calls that turn one transient API blip into a filed issue; plus suggestions on stale `now`/negative tag ages, the 40m-of-waits vs 60m leg budget, and a missing EOF newline.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 ci.yml gate: `case` branches swapped vs the documented design (comment1) — blocking
- ⚠️ integration `if` `!= 'false'` + empty-output hole; release-only alarm bypasses grace; unguarded poll calls (comments 2–4)
- 💡 stale `now` after waits; leg-budget math; EOF newline (comments 5–7)

**Next Steps**:
1. Swap the gate branches: package red → `dart_ok=false` (deferred fail), platform red → keep `dart_ok=true`, fail the aggregate after export; update the test pins that enshrine the current pattern
2. Gate the release-only alarm behind the grace window + spaced re-read; harden poll-loop `gh` calls with retry/continue
3. Note: acceptance #1 (pub.dev serves ≥1.0.521) is correctly disclosed as out of scope; the removal of the never-cut-tag wedge backstop is a deliberate tradeoff that now relies entirely on `auto_release.sh`'s own wedge alarm — worth a line in `docs/ci.md`

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the dart-only gate is inverted — the exact starvation this PR fixes still happens**

The documented design (PR description, the comments below, and the test reason strings) is: *platform/native/PTY legs "cannot redden `dart_ok`" — only package legs may redden it*. The implementation does the opposite — **the two `case` branches are swapped**:

- **Platform leg red** (this branch) sets `dart_ok=false` → the publish job's `needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true'` is false → **publish skips**. The v1.0.520 shape (red `pty-integration-linux` shard on the push twin) produces byte-for-byte the same outcome as the old result-based gate. Fix #2 is a no-op as implemented.
- **Package leg red** hits `fail` inside the loop, so the step exits **before** `echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` ever runs → the exported output is **empty**, not `false`.

Simulated against the step body verbatim:

```text
A: PTY leg red      → exported [dart_ok=false] → publish SKIPS (starvation persists), smoke skips
B: package leg red  → exported [] (nothing)    → publish SKIPS (ok), but smoke RUNS (see the integration-if comment)
```

To implement the documented behavior: in the loop, **package** legs must set `dart_ok=false` (deferred — do not `fail` inside the loop), and **platform** legs must leave `dart_ok=true` (track a separate `platform_red=true`); then export `dart_ok`, and fail the aggregate afterwards if either `dart_ok != true` or `platform_red`. That keeps the aggregate red (branch protection unchanged) while letting the push twin publish.

Note: `test/release_flow_race_test.dart`'s new pins assert the swapped pattern list verbatim ("every platform/native/PTY leg must be publish-exempt" while pinning exactly the list that reddens it) — they must be updated together with this fix, otherwise CI re-enshrines the bug.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `dart_ok != 'false'` lets the smoke run on a package-red (doomed) run — empty output ≠ `false`**

When a **package** leg is red, the gate step `fail`s before exporting `dart_ok`, so `needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok` is `''`, not `'false'`. This `if` therefore evaluates `'' != 'false'` → **true**, and the 20-minute real-provider smoke (real `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/… spend) runs on a tag run whose publish can never start (`dart_ok == 'true'` is false for `''`).

This contradicts the comment right below ("dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the publish it gates cannot run anyway") — that only holds for the platform-red path, where `dart_ok=false` is actually exported.

Two clean fixes (either suffices; do the first if you take the comment1 fix):
1. Export `dart_ok=false` for package-red too (deferred fail) — then `!= 'false'` behaves as documented.
2. Make this condition `!= 'true'` so the smoke runs only when the pure-Dart verdict is explicitly green.

The publish job is unaffected either way (it requires `== 'true'`), so this is wasted-runner/LLM-spend plus comment-accuracy, not a publish-safety bug.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "only release-event run(s)" alarm fires on the first read, bypassing the grace window — reintroduces the #1189 false-alarm class**

The grace window (AC1) exists precisely because a freshly pushed tag's ci.yml run can lag **minutes** in API visibility (#1189: tag 05:32, verify read "no run" at 05:35, healthy run completed 05:37). For PAT-pushed tags, release-tag publishes the GitHub Release essentially concurrently with the tag push, so the **release twin can become API-visible while the push twin has not registered yet**. In that window this branch alarms `never triggered (only release-event run(s) exist …)`, exits 1, and the daily self-files an issue — a false alarm of exactly the class this PR exists to kill. The grace `in_flight` skip is now only reachable when *no* runs at all exist, and the same bypass repeats on the second read (line 205).

Suggested fix: only arm the release-only alarm **past the grace window and after the spaced re-read** — i.e. move both `any_run_of` checks to after the `tag_age -lt grace` / re-read logic (a young release-only list → neutral `in_flight`; an old one → alarm). Also note `workflow_dispatch` runs on the tag ref land in this same alarm but pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC — the message text ("only release-event run(s)") would be wrong there; consider "non-push run(s)".

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: unguarded `gh run view` inside the 30-minute poll loop — one transient API failure aborts the leg as an error**

Under `set -euo pipefail`, a single transient `gh`/network failure (502, blip, secondary rate limit) on this line kills the script mid-wait, fails the leg, and the report job files "[daily-publish] pub.dev leg failed" — a false alarm re-introduced through the new polling path (up to 90 sequential API calls per wait, ×2 waits). Everywhere else the script defends against this (three spaced pub.dev reads, `curl --retry 3`, the AC1 re-read); this new loop is the least fault-tolerant network call in the file.

Suggested fix: tolerate failed polls as "still pending" and only alarm/skip on budget lapse:

```bash
if ! status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null); then
  echo "transient gh failure polling run $run_id (attempt $attempt/$attempts)"
  attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
  continue
fi
```

(The follow-up `conclusion=$(gh run view …)` after the loop has the same exposure but is pre-existing; hardening it too while you are here would be cheap.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `now` is sampled once at script start — tag ages go stale (even negative) after the waits**

`now=$(date +%s)` (line 113) is fixed, but `read_tag_age` is called again inside this appear-wait loop. If the tag is cut *during* the wait, `tag_age = now - creatordate` goes **negative** (the tag is newer than the snapshot). Downstream the grace check `[ "$tag_age" -lt "$grace" ]` then renders notices like `v1.0.521 exists (-540s old < 900s grace)` and takes the neutral-skip path — fail-safe direction, but the negative age is confusing in the leg notice/su…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

    timeout-minutes: 5

      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"

          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"

          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"

          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"

          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}

          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}

        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).

integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Issue #551: the ONLY tag-only LLM job — a small provider smoke.
      # `--tags "integration && llm"` selects the real-provider files
      # (anthropic / google / openrouter / ollama round-trips; copilot,
      # chatgpt-codex and subagent-real-model self-skip without their
      # creds). The 50-file integration suite itself runs per-PR now
      # (integration-mock + nightly pty-integration): tag CI no longer
      # gates releases on it, publish waits on this smoke instead.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart test --tags "integration && llm"
        run: dart test --tags "integration && llm"

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Install quickjs-ng
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs" \
            https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs/releases/download/v0.16.2/qjs-linux-x86_64
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: dart test --tags integration (qjs engine suites)
        run: dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/

  publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    #
    # #1368, two changes:
    # 1. PUSH-EVENT TAGS ONLY. pub.dev trusted publishing accepts OIDC tokens
    #    from push and workflow_dispatch events ONLY — there is no
    #    release-event option (owner verified the pub.dev console). The old
    #    release arm made the release-event twin of every tag ATTEMPT the
    #    publish whenever the push twin had not uploaded — pub.dev rejected
    #    the token's event claim and the leg died "Authentication failed!"
    #    (exit 65) on every release since the gate graph grew legs that can
    #    redden the push twin. The v0.1.370-402 era this arm once covered
    #    (API-created lightweight tags with no push event) is gone: every tag
    #    is PAT-pushed annotated (release-tag/auto_release), so the push twin
    #    always exists. A release-only tag would now skip publish and the
    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate

# check (gh-1192). Extracted verbatim from the inline step in
