# when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window; or the
  # release-tag job has not cut the tag off a fresh bump yet) is classified
  # «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh — a neutral skip
  # (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled daily re-verifies.
  # The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml run» error one minute
  # before the healthy run completed (#1189, false alarm).

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

#                         · the tag is not cut yet but the bump commit is
#                           on main (release-tag pending)
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)»
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

# Tag presence + age. creatordate = the annotated tag's tagger date (the
# moment release-tag cut it); a lightweight tag falls back to its commit date.

+          tagPresent: false, bumpAge: const Duration(hours: 10, minutes: 33));
+          tagAge: const Duration(minutes: 20),
+          tagAge: const Duration(hours: 2),
+          bumpAge: const Duration(seconds: 90),
===
  # Push run went green but pub.dev still serves $published — not
  # recoverable by rerunning.
  echo "::error::tag run for $tag succeeded but pub.dev still serves $published — publish did not upload. Manual publish needed (see issue)."
  exit 1
fi

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)»
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

#                         · the tag is not cut yet but the bump commit is
#                           on main (release-tag pending)
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)»
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

# Tag presence + age. creatordate = the annotated tag's tagger date (the
# moment release-tag cut it); a lightweight tag falls back to its commit date.

  # Push run went green but pub.dev still serves $published — not

  echo "::error::tag run for $tag succeeded but pub.dev still serves $published — publish did not upload. Manual publish needed (see issue)."
  exit 1
fi

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

- `publishable_run_of`: `map(select(.event == "push" or .event == "workflow_dispatch")) | .[0]` — newest push|dispatch run.
- ci.yml publish `if`: `github.event_name == 'push'` — dispatch runs skip publish.

- The manual fix in `never_triggered`: "or run ci.yml on the tag ref" — with publish `if` requiring push, a dispatched run will NOT publish. So the manual advice itself is partially wrong even independent of the selection logic! Actually wait — this advice pre-dates the PR? Let me check main's version of that message.

From the diff, the old code had:
```
-  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered. Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
```
Yes — "run ci.yml on the tag ref" advice is pre-existing. But under the OLD workflow (with the release arm), a dispatched run on the tag... the old publish if was push-or-release tag → dispatch still didn't match. Hmm, so the advice was already questionable before. But now the PR's own `publishable_run_of` treats dispatch runs as recovery-eligible/recovery targets, making the wrongness load-bearing: the script will actively SELECT a dispatch run for classification/recovery believing it can publish, when ci.yml will skip publish on it. Previously the script only looked at the newest run regardless of event (no selection), so the dispatch aspect wasn't encoded in logic.

Scenario worth flagging: push twin failed (publish job red) → operator follows advice, dispatches ci.yml on the tag → next daily: newest publishable run = the dispatch run → suppose the dispatch run went green (publish skipped — it always skips on dispatch) → conclusion=success → "publish did not upload" alarm (loud, manual publish needed) — acceptable-ish. Suppose the dispatch run failed elsewhere → rerun --failed the DISPATCH run → publish still skipped → green → next day "publish did not upload". The failed PUSH twin (the only recoverable one) is never rerun. Result: recovery permanently targets the wrong twin; each cycle wastes a day. Eventually a human reads "manual publish needed". So: no silent failure, but a real logic inconsistency between the selection predicate and the workflow's publish condition — IMPORTANT.

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)»
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

# Tag presence + age. creatordate = the annotated tag's tagger date (the
# moment release-tag cut it); a lightweight tag falls back to its commit date.

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi

conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then

  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The headline "dart-only publish gate" is inverted: platform/PTY legs are the ones that set `dart_ok=false` (so a red PTY shard still skips the publish — the v1.0.519–521 starvation persists unchanged), while package-red legs `fail` before `dart_ok` is ever exported (empty ≠ `'false'`), which makes the Provider smoke run on doomed runs. Three important issues: the new "only release-event run(s)" alarm bypasses the #1189 grace window and can false-alarm in the release-twin-first visibility race; the 30-min terminal-wait poll loop makes unguarded `gh run view` calls that turn one transient API blip into a filed issue; plus suggestions on stale `now`/negative tag ages, the 40m-of-waits vs 60m leg budget, and a missing EOF newline.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 ci.yml gate: `case` branches swapped vs the documented design (comment1) — blocking
- ⚠️ integration `if` `!= 'false'` + empty-output hole; release-only alarm bypasses grace; unguarded poll calls (comments 2–4)
- 💡 stale `now` after waits; leg-budget math; EOF newline (comments 5–7)

**Next Steps**:
1. Swap the gate branches: package red → `dart_ok=false` (deferred fail), platform red → keep `dart_ok=true`, fail the aggregate after export; update the test pins that enshrine the current pattern
2. Gate the release-only alarm behind the grace window + spaced re-read; harden poll-loop `gh` calls with retry/continue
3. Note: acceptance #1 (pub.dev serves ≥1.0.521) is correctly disclosed as out of scope; the removal of the never-cut-tag wedge backstop is a deliberate tradeoff that now relies entirely on `auto_release.sh`'s own wedge alarm — worth a line in `docs/ci.md`

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking issue: the new `release-twin-only` regression test fails deterministically (fixture tag defaults to 60s old, inside the 900s grace window, so the script correctly skips and exits 0 — the suite, which gates this PR, is red; verified locally: 50 pass / 1 fail, exit 1). So the manual-fix message is now actively misleading: following it cannot fix the state and produces a NEW alarm class.

   - State: no tag run registered past grace (or only non-push runs). The message: "re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
   - Re-push: creates a fresh push event → new push run → publishable → fix works. ✓
   - Dispatch ci.yml on the tag ref: creates a workflow_dispatch run → publish job skips (requires push) → no publish; and with push-only selection, the script never treats it as publishable. So the advice's second half is useless.

So it's not silent, not a behavior bug — it's message accuracy. Previously I folded this into the IMPORTANT dispatch comment ("Then also stop advising…"). The author fixed the selection half but not the message half. This is now a leftover fragment of a resolved thread. Per the verdict rules: new suggestion-level nits on a re-review should converge to APPROVE; but is this suggestion-level or IMPORTANT? It's an operator-facing runbook line that wastes one manual action (dispatch → nothing happens → re-push anyway). The re-push works; no alarm is silenced; recovery isn't misdirected anymore (push-only selection means the dispatch run can't hijack recovery). The remaining harm: an operator following advice #2 wastes a dispatch and might conclude the fix didn't work — but advice #1 is right there and works.

#                         · the tag is not cut yet but the bump commit is

#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)»
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

# Tag presence + age. creatordate = the annotated tag's tagger date (the
# moment release-tag cut it); a lightweight tag falls back to its commit date.

  # Push run went green but pub.dev still serves $published — not
  # recoverable by rerunning.
  echo "::error::tag run for $tag succeeded but pub.dev still serves $published — publish did not upload. Manual publish needed (see issue)."
  exit 1
fi

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

#   «never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)»
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version

# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}

}

# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then

# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +

# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then

  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `publishable_run_of` treats `workflow_dispatch` runs as recovery targets, but ci.yml's publish `if` fires on `push` events only — a dispatch twin can never publish**

Line 142 selects `event == "push" or event == "workflow_dispatch"` as "publishable", and the comment says both "carry OIDC tokens pub.dev accepts". True at the pub.dev layer — but **this repo's publish job requires the push event**: `github.event_name == 'push'` in the new publish `if` (ci.yml). A rerun keeps the original event, so `gh run rerun` of a dispatch twin re-runs with `workflow_dispatch` → the publish job is skipped by its `if` → the run goes green without uploading → the next daily reads `conclusion=success` + pub.dev behind → **"publish did not upload"**.

Two ways this bites:

1. **It steals selection from the real twin.** `publishable_run_of` picks the *newest* push|dispatch run. If a push twin failed and an operator then dispatches ci.yml on the tag ref — which this script's own manual-fix message recommends (`never_triggered`: "…or run ci.yml on the tag ref") — the dispatch run becomes the newest "publishable" run. Every subsequent daily then classifies/reruns the **dispatch** twin (whose publish is structurally skipped) instead of the failed push twin (the only recoverable one). Recovery loops wrong until a human publishes manually.
2. **The alarm text mis-states the repo's own gate.** "only release-event run(s) exist — pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch runs only" implies a dispatch run would have published; under the current publish `if` it would not.

Two one-line fixes (either):

- **Match the script to the workflow** (my preference, also matches the file header's "The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job… tag-push runs"): select `event == "push"` only, and word the alarm "…ci.yml's publish job fires on push-tag events only". Then also stop advising "run ci.yml on the tag ref" in the manual-fix text — that advice can never produce a publish under the push-only `if`.
- **Match the workflow to the script**: drop `github.event_name == 'push'` from the publish `if` (keep the tag-ref check) so a dispatch twin really is publishable — pub.dev accepts dispatch-event OIDC per this PR's own research, and the operator runbook then works as advertised.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the budget comment presents the worst cases as alternatives ("or"), but they can stack — real worst case ≈ 55m against the 60m leg ceiling**

The header reads: "appear-wait 10m + terminal-wait 15m = 25m, **or** appear-wait 10m + bounded rerun watch 20m + post-rerun verify poll 10m ≈ 40m". Those are not exclusive: a tag that appears mid-wait, a push run that flips terminal at minute ~14 of the terminal wait, a failing rerun, and a slow pub.dev CDN stack all four:

```text
appear-wait 600s + terminal-wait ~900s + rerun watch 1200s + post-rerun poll 600s ≈ 3300s (55m)
```

plus git fetches, three spaced pub.dev reads and the rerun sleep — leaving roughly 5m of headroom on the `Leg: pub.dev` 60m ceiling. Exceeding it yields a **cancelled** leg, which the report files as a watcher death — the exact end-to-end guarantee this comment promises to protect. The path is unlikely but real (that's the same class the 15m resize was meant to fix).

Cheapest fix is truth-in-commenting: state the stacked worst case (~55m, ~5m headroom) so nobody "sizes up" `RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS` back to 1800 on the strength of the 40m figure. If you want real headroom instead, trim the post-rerun poll (`30 × 20s` → `20 × 15s`) or bound the watch at 900s.

#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects

#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still

# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

# moment release-tag cut it); a lightweight tag falls back to its commit date.

echo "tag run $run_id concluded $conclusion — re-running its failed jobs (keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims)"
# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"

# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$rstatus" != "completed" ]; then
  # The bounded watch lapsed (or the API blipped) with the rerun still
  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"
